checks.claim: Windows failure (a): KeyError 'HOME' at import in getnml2.py when HOME unset
checks.reported_value: Under PowerShell without HOME, crash at import with KeyError 'HOME' in omv/engines/getnml2.py
checks.verified_value: Reproduced in PowerShell (HOME absent) and in Git Bash with 'env -u HOME': even 'omv --version' dies with KeyError 'HOME' from getnml2.py module-level 'install_root = os.environ["HOME"]', exit 1. Root cause: omv_util.main() has set_env_vars() that copies USERPROFILE into HOME on Windows, but it runs after the module imports that already read HOME
checks.method: PowerShell: Remove-Item Env:HOME; omv.exe --version; Git Bash: env -u HOME omv.exe --version; read omv_util.py set_env_vars and getnml2.py

checks.claim: Windows failure (b): Git Bash WinError 2 spawning pylems, root cause not isolated
checks.reported_value: Under Git Bash the engine subprocess raised WinError 2; root cause not isolated
checks.verified_value: Root cause isolated and not shell-specific: PyLEMS_NeuroML2 calls subprocess.check_output(['pylems', ...]) by bare name, so 'pylems' must be on PATH. In Git Bash with the venv Scripts folder NOT on PATH the test fails with WinError 2 (exit 1); with the venv Scripts folder prepended to PATH the same test passes in Git Bash (both experiments, exit 0)
checks.method: Git Bash runs RUN1 (no venv on PATH) and RUN2 (PATH=venv/Scripts:$PATH), logs in scratchpad/m0/verify-omv/run/ex9/run1.log, run2.log

checks.claim: Engine version pinning via --engine=NAME:VERSION installs that engine version (e.g. jNeuroML:v0.12.3, jNeuroML_NEURON:8.2.7)
checks.reported_value: --engine=NAME:VERSION first installs that engine version; OMV gives NeuroSem engine version pinning
checks.verified_value: Not reliable. _install_engine handles NAME:VERSION per engine: for jNeuroML it calls JNeuroMLEngine.install(None), dropping the version, so 'jNeuroML:v0.12.3' does not pin jNeuroML. For jNeuroML_NEURON the version goes to the NEURON install (a NEURON version). jLEMS, PyLEMS, Py_neuroConstruct, genesis, PyNN_NEURON and PyLEMS_NeuroML2 (when NeuroML2 is missing) raise when a version is given. Engines with no install branch (e.g. jNeuroML_validate, PyNN_NeuroML) print 'Code not implemented yet' and exit 1. If the engine is already installed, nothing checks that the installed version matches
checks.method: Read _install_engine in omv_util.py, jneuroml.py, jneuromlnrn.py, getnrn.py, engine.py in installed 0.4.0

corrections_summary: Most version, date, license, dependency, issue, engine-list, CLI and tolerance claims hold. Corrections: (1) CI coverage is understated. Besides ci.yml (Python 3.12, ubuntu-22.04) there is ci_versions.yml, which tests Python 3.9-3.13 on ubuntu-latest, macos-14 and macos-latest. Still no Windows runner. (2) The Windows Git Bash WinError 2 is not shell-specific. Its cause is that PyLEMS_NeuroML2 spawns bare 'pylems', which must be on PATH, and the test passes in Git Bash once the venv Scripts folder is on PATH. So 'passed only under PowerShell' is wrong; the real needs are HOME defined, the engine executable on PATH and UTF-8 output. (3) The 'jNeuroML auto-installer uses wget/unzip' claim is stale. getjnml.install_jnml has no callers in 0.4.0, and the jNeuroML engine installs pyNeuroML with a bare 'pip'. (4) NAME:VERSION engine pinning is not reliable. The version is dropped for jNeuroML ('jNeuroML:v0.12.3' does not pin jNeuroML), means the NEURON version for jNeuroML_NEURON, raises or exits for several engines, and is never checked once an engine is installed. (5) The mtime freshness check covers only the spike times, spike rate and timeseries analyzers. Resting, input resistance and activation-variable analyzers can read stale files. (6) The MEP 'protocol' entry is required, not optional, in OMV's own Rx schema, so OMV's example MEPs fail validation once the schema types exist. (7) The '0 to about 3e-3' tolerance range is contradicted by OMV's own 0.004099 tolerance. The KeyError 'HOME' crash is confirmed, with a root cause the report did not name: set_env_vars copies USERPROFILE to HOME but runs after the imports that read HOME. The validate-mep failure also affects installs from the sdist, which resolves one of the report's open uncertainties.
additional_findings: Second CI workflow 'Test across versions' (ci_versions.yml): Python 3.9-3.13 x ubuntu-latest/macos-14/macos-latest, pytest in omv/test, jNeuroML_NEURON tests and an --exit-zero broken-test step; monthly cron on day 15. No Windows runner in any OMV workflow. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/.github/workflows/ci_versions.yml

README quick-install command 'pip install osb-model-validation' does not work: that name is not registered on PyPI (JSON API 404; pip reports no matching distribution). The real distribution is OSBModelValidation. Documents and setup scripts should use the real name, and the unregistered lookalike name is a possible typosquatting risk. https://pypi.org/pypi/osb-model-validation/json ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/README.md

License audit flag: required dependency pyrx 0.3.0 (last PyPI release 2013-12-17) declares license 'GPLv2' in PyPI metadata. Its GitHub repo uniphil/pyrx is archived (last push 2013-12-18) and the GitHub license API finds no license file. docopt 0.6.2 is MIT with its last release on 2014-06-16. Both are old and unmaintained; the GPLv2 declaration in an LGPL-3.0-only tool's dependency chain needs review in LICENSE_AUDIT.md. https://pypi.org/pypi/pyrx/json ; https://api.github.com/repos/uniphil/pyrx ; https://pypi.org/pypi/docopt/json
PyLEMS (used by the PyLEMS_NeuroML2 engine) is 0.6.9 on PyPI with license LGPL-3.0-only. https://pypi.org/pypi/pylems/json

Windows HOME bug root cause: omv_util.set_env_vars() copies USERPROFILE into HOME on Windows, but omv_util first imports omv.engines, whose getnml2.py reads os.environ['HOME'] at module import. Any OMV command, even --version, crashes when HOME is unset. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/omv/omv_util.py

Auto-install uses a bare 'pip' executable (omv/common/inout.py pip_install builds ['pip', 'install', pkg]), not sys.executable -m pip. If the venv is not first on PATH, engine auto-installs can go into a different Python (e.g. a system interpreter). The PyLEMS engine install also sets PYLEMS_HOME under $HOME. NeuroSem should pre-install pinned engines and treat any OMV auto-install as a failure. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/omv/common/inout.py

Analyzer edge case: before any tolerance comparison, OMVAnalyzer.__call__ returns False when observed or expected is a Python list containing a falsy element. So an MEP expected list with 0 or 0.0 (e.g. a spike at t=0 or a zero value) fails regardless of tolerance. Probe: identical lists [0.0, 10.0] at tolerance 0.5 failed; [0.1, 10.0] passed. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/omv/analyzers/analyzer.py

validate-mep exits with code 0 even when the document is invalid (it prints False), so it cannot gate CI even where the schema types are present. OMV's own .test.ex9.mep is invalid under its schema because experiment.yaml requires 'protocol'. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/omv/schemata/types/experiment.yaml

Installing from the 0.4.0 sdist also omits omv/schemata/types. setup.cfg package_data 'schemata/*' is not recursive and include_package_data is not set; MANIFEST.in 'recursive-include omv/schemata *' affects only the sdist. The same setup.cfg is used by git installs (as in OSB omv-ci.yml), so they are expected to behave the same (git install itself not executed). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/setup.cfg ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/MANIFEST.in

Unit-scaling trap for fixtures: OMV's own .test.ex9.pylems.omt scales both columns of the V experiment by 1000 and compares against MEP times like 2440.0 and 39110.0. OMT 'scaling' factors are ad hoc per test, so NeuroSem should not reuse OMV MEP numbers as physical-unit ground truth without checking units. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/utilities/tests/.test.ex9.pylems.omt

A failed engine run is still reported per observable: the spike analyzer reports a missing datafile and fails, but PyLEMS_NeuroML2.run catches generic exceptions and sets returncode -1 without re-raising. The tally, not an exception, carries the failure, and the overall exit code is 1 only because the assertion fails. NeuroSem's 'non-executable' classification should read the engine return code and the missing output, not rely on OMV exceptions. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/master/omv/engines/pylemsnml2.py

Maintenance evidence: latest scheduled 'Continuous builds' run on master was 2026-09-01 (success); the repository has active dependabot updates (runs 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-08). https://api.github.com/repos/OpenSourceBrain/osb-model-validation/actions/runs?branch=master&per_page=3
